lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: North America stayed soft through PepsiCo's Q3 (mid-June to 5 Sept). US gasoline averaged about $3.98/gal over the quarter against $3.13 a year earlier, so the Q2 headwind management blamed did not ease. JPMorgan (09-29) says tracked-channel data shows NA underperforming management's plan. PepsiCo is partly reversing its February price cuts after they failed to grow sales (Bloomberg, 09-24). Read: PFNA organic about -2% rather than the -1% Zacks models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09: revenue beat with PFNA organic -2% and NA organic -0.5%, stock -3.26%. 2026-04-16: PFNA organic +1% with volume +2%, stock +2.28% (baseline history; Q1/Q2 2026 releases).

findings.finding: Input costs moved sharply against PepsiCo after the 9 July call that put FY2026 EPS 'towards the low end'. Brent 78.0 to 100.6 (+29%). ULSD diesel 3.66 to 4.57 (+25%, and +96% against the Q4-2025 average), landing in a 16-week North America Q4 that has to deliver about +9-10% constant-currency EPS. Corn +17%, sugar +38%, 10-year yield +70bp to 5.27%. This raises the odds the release trims FY core constant-currency EPS below +4%. Offsets: about 1 point of tariff refunds already being received, Q3 FX of about +1 point, record productivity, and peers GIS (09-23) and CAG (09-30) both held their full-year guides in the same tape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-04-24 guidance cut: -4.89%. 2025-02-04 weak guide: -4.51%. 2026-07-09 reaffirmed with a low-end tilt: -3.26%. 2025-07-16 reaffirmed after a cut, on low expectations: +7.45% (baseline history).

findings.finding: Q3 core EPS should meet or slightly beat the $2.30 consensus. It is carried by the IEEPA tariff refunds the CFO placed in Q3 (about 1 point of FY EPS), which the Q2 10-Q says PepsiCo had already 'begun to receive', plus about a 1-point FX tailwind in June-August (y/y: MXN +8.7%, BRL +7.1%, CNY +6.1%, ZAR +8.7%, COP +23%, against EUR -1.0%, CAD -2.2%, TRY -14.7%, INR -9.4%). This is a low-quality beat, inside what management already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09: core EPS $2.20 vs $2.21, a one-cent miss, stock -3.26%. 2025-10-08 (Q3 2025): beat with guide held, +4.23% (baseline history).

outside_window.finding: PepsiCo promised a 'comprehensive update' on an integrated North America supply-chain and go-to-market model for late 2026, and the CEO said on 9 July 'later in the year, early next year'. Most likely it comes after the Oct 8 window, at Q4 results or a separate event. Worth about +1 if it carries hard savings numbers.
Low-to-mid single-digit price increases on grocery-size Doritos/Ruffles/SunChips, some sodas and Tostitos/Fritos dips, taking effect at end-2026/early-2027. Already public, so worth 0 in the window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (a refund is noise next to the guide; a finding inside what management guided goes toward 0): F3 (Q3 EPS) cut from +0.2 to +0.1. The beat rests on a pre-announced tariff refund and FX.

findings.finding: The FQ2 revenue guide most likely lands at a $100-104m midpoint. RGP's own per-day run rate from the FQ1 guide gives $96.7-103.6m. That is around the ~$102m middle estimate but below the $105.6m headline consensus, which a $115.0m outlier inflates, so the guide is likely to print as 'below consensus'. Staffing data since July 22 (ASA +3.3-5.5% y/y, Robert Half guiding Jul-Sep talent solutions +1-5%, Korn Ferry interim 'significant lift') make a July-style step-down below ~$98m less likely than the tape implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Next-quarter guide: Jan 2026 -14.6% and Jul 2026 -18.4% when the guide stepped down after in-line quarters; Apr 2026 -1.4% on a roughly flat FQ4 guide ($104-109m vs FQ3 $107.9m), after which the stock rallied ~35% into June.

findings.finding: Cash at Aug 29 2026 is likely ~$62-72m (central ~$68m), down ~$14m from $82.4m in one quarter, about 11% of the $127m market cap. FQ1 operating cash flow is negative every year (-$7.8m in FQ1 FY26). This quarter adds guided negative adjusted EBITDA (~-$4.7m), the $2.4m June dividend, the COO's $1.65m lump sum, the former CEO's monthly severance installments (~$1.5m a quarter) and a $2.26m RIF accrual, all disclosed in the 10-K.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned on cash alone. The July 2026 -18.4% coincided with the covenant non-compliance disclosure and the move to a secured borrowing-base revolver, so liquidity was part of that reaction.

findings.finding: The CFO who resigned on Sept 1, three days after the quarter closed, left to become CFO of Xponential Fitness at a $550k base salary effective Oct 19 2026 (Xponential 8-K filed 2026-09-08). It was a career move, not a signal about the quarter. RGP lost ~9% over Sept 3-4 around the announcement and has not recovered, so a clean release removes an overhang.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RGP fell from $4.46 (Sept 2) to $4.04 (Sept 4) on the resignation news; no prior print involved a CFO change.

outside_window.finding: The next $0.07 dividend decision falls ~2-3 weeks after the print, on the 2026 cadence (announced Jan 28, Apr 28, Aug 11), so around late October. With cash heading to ~$68m and adjusted EBITDA negative, a cut or suspension at that decision is a real risk (probability ~25-30%) on a 7.6% yield.
Annual meeting Oct 22 2026 votes on adding 1,000,000 shares (2.9% of outstanding) to the 2020 Performance Incentive Plan and more ESPP shares; Carlile becomes Chair and the board shrinks to six.

lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a company-level number beats an industry proxy): Q1 guidance finding moved from -0.3 to -0.5, because RGP's own per-day arithmetic ($96.7-103.6m) outweighs the ASA, Robert Half and Korn Ferry proxies that had offset it, and RGP's -18% decline against Robert Half's flat F&A shows weak transmission

Lesson 1 and 'documents beat inference': Q5 cash-burn finding moved from -0.8 to -0.5; it is a projection from the 10-K and XBRL rather than a reported number, and no print in the baseline traded on cash

Lesson 6: the FQ2 revenue bar has one source (Yahoo, with a $115m outlier), so the guide finding stays capped small; every filed finding resolves on 2026-10-07/08, while the dividend decision (~late Oct) and the Oct 22 meeting stay in outside_window

Lessons 2, 4, 8 and 9 changed nothing: no one-off, the July revolver is an undrawn backstop rather than a financing sign, no confirmed unpriced company number, no segment-only finding; the CFO finding stays at +0.2 and abs_move_pct stays at 9.0
